 Judgment
MFA No.8369/2011 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation.
2. MFA Crob. No.121/2013 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed by the learned Commissioner.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the claimant has sustained injuries out of and in the course of employment under respondent No.1-owner of the lorry bearing No.KA-16/A-8582 on 02.01.2009 at about 12.00 noon near Chitradurga while he was proceeding in a lorry as Cleaner.

4. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
The Branch Manager vs Sri. Arif on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192982418/
3 5.
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that in respect of the grounds raised in the appeal memorandum, the judgment and award is to be set-aside.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the compensation awarded by the learned Commissioner is meager one.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.

7. This Court while admitting the appeal on 10.02.2022, has framed the following substantial questions of law:
i. Whether the rate of interest awarded by the Commissioner is in accordance with law?
ii. Whether the loss of earning capacity assessed by the learned Commissioner is proper?

8. Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the following substantial question of law arises for consideration:
Whether the parameters held by the learned Commissioner in assessing the quantum of compensation is correct?
9.
In the present case, as per medical records, the claimant has sustained intertrochanteric fracture of left femur and comminuted volar barton fracture of left radius.
10. The doctor had stated that the claimant was operated for intertrochanteric fracture by fixation with DHS.

The doctor had stated that the claimant had sustained permanent physical disability to the extent of 69% to the left lower limb and 20% of permanent physical disability to his left upper limb but the learned Commissioner has taken only 25% disability as 'loss of earnings'.
The learned Commissioner is not correct in assessing the permanent disability at 25% only.
The case is under unscheduled injuries.
There is no clear evidence of the doctor whether the claimant has suffered permanent total disability or permanent partial disability.
The case can be considered as permanent partial disability at least to the extent.

Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant and he was Cleaner in the lorry, it is just and proper to take 40% as permanent partial disability.
The learned Commissioner has committed error in taking monthly wage at Rs.2,460/- but as per Section 4-A of the EC Act, the monthly wage of Rs.4,000/- p.m. is taken into consideration.
The claimant was aged 32 years old.
Therefore, the relevant factor is 197.06.

Therefore, the 'loss of earning capacity due to disability' is hereby re-assessed and quantified as under:
Rs.4000 x 60/100 x 197.06 x 40/100 = Rs.1,89,178/-
The Branch Manager vs Sri. Arif on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192982418/
4
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.1,89,178/- is awarded under the head 'loss of earning capacity due to disability'.

11. The Tribunal has committed error in awarding interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization and thereafter at the rate of 12% p.a., is not correct.
The claimant is entitled interest at the rate of 12% p.a., from the date of the accident till realization.

IN MFA CROB. NO.121/2013:
12.

This Court while admitting the cross objection on 10.02.2022, has framed the following substantial questions of law:
iii. Whether the Commissioner had jurisdiction to entertain the claim petition and conduct the proceedings in view of the amended Section 20 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923?
iv.

Whether the 'employer' 'employee' relationship has been established in this case?"
13.

Further, upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the following substantial questions of law arises for consideration:
i. Whether upon failure of duties to be performed by the employer, the statutory right of the claimant is affected?
ii.

Whether, under facts and circumstances tendered in the case, what would be the extent of liability of payment of compensation and interest on part of the insurance company and employer as per Section 4-A of the EC Act?
14. The word workmen is deleted and in its place the word "Employees" is inserted to the Workmen Compensation Act, 1923 (erstwhile) w.e.f., 18.01.2010 by way of amendment as amended by Act 45/2000.
The only amendment is made to incorporate employee in the place of workmen.
Admittedly, in the present case, the claimant was Cleaner by profession.
Therefore, there is no merit in the ground raised that the proceeding is vitiated.
15. Section 134C of the MV Act stipulates upon owner and driver to give information to the Insurance Company regarding factum of accident and other particulars.
If it is not complied with then rights of the claimant is not vitiated.
The duties cast on the driver and owner are different and right of the claimant is different.

If someone fails in his duty that cannot affect the rights of - 10 - The Branch Manager vs Sri. Arif on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192982418/
5 the other party.
The statutory right is always the right conferred and that is not fluctuated according to failure in performance of duties.

Therefore, just because the owner/driver have failed to intimate the insurance company regarding the factum of accident and other particulars that cannot deprived the statutory right of the claimant for seeking compensation.
Section 168(4) of MV Act stipulates that the information received by the police regarding the accident can be treated itself as a claim petition.
Therefore, just because the police have not submitted the accident information report to the learned Commissioner that cannot affect the statutory right of the claimant for seeking compensation.

Just because the employer is a owner of the lorry and claimant is cleaner and if employer has not maintaining wage register and books as per Section 18 of the Minimum Wage Act,
1959 and Rule 29 of the Karnataka Minimum wage Rules is not ground to deny compensation to the claimant.
If employer fails in his duty to maintain wage register and books and that cannot deprive the rights of the claimant for seeking - 11 - compensation.
Therefore, the ground raised in this regard also not hampered the claim of the claimant.
16. Before the learned Commissioner/Tribunal, the evidence can be tendered in the form of affidavit by way of examination-in-chief as per Section 23 of the Act and rule 41 of the Rules.
17. It is proved that as per Section 4-A of the EC act, it is duty cast on the employer to pay compensation to the admitted extent.

Just because the employer has failed to pay compensation under impression that the vehicle is insured with the insurance company, therefore, making indemnification is purely matter of contract between the insurer and the insured.

Therefore, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation as per the amount determined and if in absence of any specific stipulation regarding payment of interest then the owner shall pay the interest thereon for the determined compensation from the date of accident till realization.

Therefore, there is no merit found in the contentions urged by the learned counsel for Insurance - 12 - Company that just because the employer has failed to pay the compensation then the insurance company is not liable.
The Insurance company is liable to pay lump-sum amount as determined.
If there is a Clause in the contract of insurance to pay interest also then the Insurance Company shall pay interest.

If there is any absence in the insurance policy regarding payment of interest then the employer shall pay interest at 12% p.a., from the date of accident till realization on the determined compensation.

18. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeals are allowed-in-part.
